County Commissioners, school Off-

health-minded citizens were met

time of need. So to the farthest
out-posts, the sentinels of the pub-
lic health service—our midwives and
the registrars of vital statistics

approved equipment and procedure.

tistics and to the homes of twenty
six of the sixty midwives or those

during 1886.

townships of the county so that

eager to meet the new REQUIRE-

are quite as enthusiastic that their
own community helper shall mea-
sure up to the best to be found in
the state.

NEW YORK, August 30—Indications that smaller commission houses would vigorously battle the proposed increase in New York Stock Exchange commission rates have been plentiful of recent days.

These firms hold that the long doldrum of apathetic trading that has gripped the market since March has been harder on them than on the larger wire houses. Now, they assert, to raise fees in the face of reduced business, would impose an even heavier burden.

Arguments in favor of the increase, which would average about 30 per cent, have been based on the smaller volume, increased overhead for wages, rent and other expenses and the cost of maintaining wire systems.

Many of the larger houses have felt that, since S. E. C. regulations were imposed in an ever stricter degree their best chance of improving their volume was to seek the investment rather than smaller, or margin accounts.

The smaller firms, operating without the heavy overhead feel that in many instances they will be penalized for the higher fees.

Especially, they assert, will they lose much of the odd-lot business which has been profitable to them in the past.
